note: RS4c integration (R6.40): writes_sleeves_nobroker.json with rate limiting left ENABLED. With no Redis URL Python builds no limiter (app.py: RateLimiter(cache, ...) if cache is not None) and serves unmetered; Rust used to refuse every request with 503. Same nine cases. Review of lane writes-sleeves: the same writes with no task queue and no cache (BASKFY_REDIS_URL empty). POST /backtests with the Celery executor and no broker fails the row in the request (_why_it_cannot_start) and answers 202 status=failed; the scan routes insert their run and publish nothing; the tag correction reads no Laya answer. Run: python3 tools/parity/api_diff.py --writes --lane wslnb --smtp-port 18333 --redis-db-py 14 --redis-db-rs 15 --py-port 18331 --rs-port 18332 --cases tools/parity/api_cases/writes_sleeves_nobroker.json BASKFY_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false: Python builds no limiter without a cache, while Rust's state.rs builds one that refuses every request with 503 (a foundation divergence, reported to the integrator).
